reason: Internal: a new eval-only module and two design nodes, no production code and nothing a member of a room can observe. evals/backbone.py is the SDK-native spine for the evaluation suite: layers 3 and 4 only — obtaining the deployed Nora, isolating a case, driving one entry point, and grading an ABSENCE — with no runner, no report renderer and no outcome type, because strands-agents-evals already ships those. MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-18 against the deployed nora alias: a populated Session DOES reach a TRACE_LEVEL evaluator for the participation entry point — one trace, six spans, her real context header and tag message and send_reply tool call, and an AgentInvocationSpan, which is what the SDK's turn extractor needs. A ToolExecutionSpan is in the same trace, so the routing tier that two documents recorded as unrecoverable has its material already present. An ERROR case pointed at a model alias that does not exist landed as ERROR rather than PASS, where every built-in evaluator would have scored it a pass because it expects silence and produced silence; on the same run the SDK's own overall_score said 0.33 while the reading said one of two gradable and one ERROR. THREE THINGS THE SDK DOES THAT A READER WOULD NOT EXPECT, each found by running it: a task's returned metadata key is silently dropped, so the failure reason rides on environment_state instead and the first probe reported an instrument fault as a measurement of Nora; EvaluationOutput.label survives only in detailed_results and is absent from cases, scores and test_passes, which are the three fields anyone reaches for first; and the eval_task wrapper is synchronous and never awaits, so the async escape taken is asyncio.run inside a sync function, which forces max_workers=1 — the same serial constraint TracedHandler already imposes, arriving twice. The scenario map derives nine failure classes from the ISSUE RECORD rather than from the existing corpora and finds the coverage inverted: 75 of 150 cases grade speech-versus-silence and 23 grade grounding, while wrong-room, tool routing, empty-context and loud-failure have essentially none, and each of those four has produced a live incident. Nothing anywhere asks what she does when a tool FAILS. Four of the nine classes need no model call at all and are therefore gate-able, which is the cheapest coverage available and the suite has almost none of it. A decision is RESERVED rather than taken, because it changes what the suite is for. LIMITS: only the participation entry point was driven; the relevance gate's 40 cases remain measured-broken because Nora emits no span events; room_for, workspace_for and the teardown are layer-3 logic still living inside the layer-1 file that is to be deleted, and backbone.py imports them with a comment saying so; and the scenario classification was done by hand over one pass of the issue list, which is the weakest claim in either node.
